correctness.rationale: For every n≥2, every p_i>0 and B>0, the complete-graph Laplacian equals nI−11ᵀ. Its PSD rank-one test is exactly sum_i 1/(n+u_i−lambda)≤1 with all denominators positive. KKT determines the price-ordered clipped square-root reciprocals. A strict tangent inequality certifies unique global minimum cost for each lambda, hence unique maximal lambda for each budget. The active-set formulas, endpoint matching and C1/affine phase laws follow algebraically. Standard-library exact rational and numerical tests completed 16,146 supplementary cases; no finite test is used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The prior weighted linear importance-budget and general SDP frameworks are acknowledged as existing, as is the complete-graph equal-price solution. Distinct assessed statements are the all-arbitrary-independent-price complete-network optimal allocation, nested budget activation thresholds, uniqueness, C1 concave rate and exact final affine law. Full text of most relevant 2015, 2022, 2024 sources was compared; a 2020 related source remained abstract-only and specialist priority risk is explicitly retained. A search nonmatch alone does not establish novelty.
residual_risks: 2015 linearly weighted importance-based cost formulation is a close predecessor; the independent price coefficients and complete explicit transitions are not shown in inspected article, but could be derivable via another source.
Full text of the 2020 optimal-cost proceedings source was not accessible; its abstract is insufficient for a decisive claim-level comparison.
A specialized matrix diagonal-loading/water-filling theorem or thesis could already imply the stated formulas, despite the available published-source and result-index comparisons.

value.rationale: Independently priced pinning gains arise naturally in consensus control where actuator strengths incur different marginal costs. The exact support activation order, entry budgets, global uniqueness and C1-to-affine phase behavior give structurally useful design information unavailable from a uniform-price allocation or generic SDP statement alone. The result covers every complete-network size and every positive price vector without a preset active set.
